items.name: AutoCAD
items.tagline: Widely used DWG-based CAD for documentation, detailing, and drawing release.
items.summary: AutoCAD is a general-purpose CAD application centered on the DWG drawing format. It appears in AEC and manufacturing workflows for plans, details, and sheet sets. Licensing and vertical bundles change over time—confirm on the vendor site before purchasing.

items.name: Revit
items.tagline: Model-based AEC authoring where drawings and schedules derive from the building dataset.
items.summary: Revit supports architectural, structural, and MEP disciplines in one model-centric workflow—often paired with IFC exchange and documentation standards. Suitability varies by regional practice and LOD expectations.

items.name: Fusion 360
items.tagline: Cloud-connected MCAD spanning modeling, assemblies, CAM, electronics (where licensed).
items.summary: Fusion 360 targets product design workflows with solid/surface modeling, assemblies, visualization, and optional manufacturing tooling. Feature availability depends on subscription tier and region.

items.name: Inventor
items.tagline: Desktop MCAD focused on mechanical design, assembly modeling, and drawing production.
items.summary: Inventor is commonly used in mechanical industries for part/assembly modeling, drawings, and design automation. It complements (rather than replaces) tools like AutoCAD in many engineering offices.

items.name: Civil 3D
items.tagline: Civil engineering design environment built on the DWG platform with BIM-style objects.
items.summary: Civil 3D supports roadway, corridor, grading, pipe networks, and plan production workflows for transportation and site projects—often alongside AutoCAD skills and surveying inputs.

items.name: SOLIDWORKS
items.tagline: Popular desktop MCAD for parts, assemblies, drawings, simulation (by license).
items.summary: SOLIDWORKS is widely adopted in discrete manufacturing for conceptual design through fabrication documentation. Companion products cover simulation and PDM workflows—beyond the CAD core.

items.name: BricsCAD
items.tagline: CAD platform with strong DWG compatibility and optional BIM/MCAD modules.
items.summary: BricsCAD targets teams that need familiar DWG workflows with optional advanced modeling modules. Compare modules and licensing with your documentation and collaboration requirements.

items.name: Archicad
items.tagline: Architectural BIM modeling and documentation with strong publishing workflows.
items.summary: Archicad is common in architectural practices that want model-based documentation and coordination. OpenBIM/IFC usage depends on project standards and exchange agreements.

items.name: FreeCAD
items.tagline: Cross-platform parametric modeling with multiple workbenches and file exchange.
items.summary: FreeCAD is a free/open-source option for Part Design, assemblies (workbench-dependent), and mesh/BIM experiments. Version and workbench maturity varies—validate for your deliverable types.

items.name: Onshape
items.tagline: Full-cloud CAD with real-time collaboration and built-in PDM-style document control.
items.summary: Onshape runs in the browser with data managed in the cloud—useful for distributed teams and hardware startups. Evaluate IP policies, export controls, and offline needs against your organization rules.

items.name: GstarCAD
items.tagline: Cross-platform CAD platform that emphasizes DWG compatibility and familiar AutoCAD-style workflows.
items.summary: GstarCAD is Gstarsoft’s flagship DWG editing environment for 2D documentation and 3D modeling, including a Linux edition in recent releases. Command names, aliases, and drawing organization will feel familiar to ACAD-style users; always match help PDFs to your installed build and language pack.

items.name: GstarCAD Mechanical
items.tagline: Mechanical design add-on with library parts, BOM hooks, and drawing automation on the GstarCAD stack.
items.summary: Targets machinery and factory documentation: standard parts, hole/tolerance helpers, and mechanical-specific palettes layered on top of core GstarCAD. Compare feature lists against your legacy ACM-style drawings if you migrate projects.

items.name: GstarCAD Architecture
items.tagline: Architectural drawing environment with wall/door/window style objects and project-oriented layer conventions.
items.summary: Suited to building plans, elevations, and construction documentation when you want DWG-based AEC tools rather than a full BIM database. Coordinate deliverables with project partners on expected object types and export formats.

items.name: GstarCAD Point Cloud
items.tagline: Import and work with scan data for as-built documentation and modeling assistance inside GstarCAD.
items.summary: Used when field scans must meet CAD deliverables: registration concepts, clipping, and vector extraction depend on project scale. Use the vendor’s Point Cloud user guides for command coverage by version.

items.name: GstarCAD 365
items.tagline: Subscription-style cloud bridge for sharing drawings, sheets, and comments across teams beyond a single LAN drive.
items.summary: Positions Gstarsoft’s ecosystem for distributed review: pair with desktop GstarCAD for authoring and use web/mobile viewers where appropriate. Confirm account, region, and retention policies on the official product pages.

items.name: GstarBIM
items.tagline: All-in-one BIM-oriented environment aimed at architects and interior designers in Gstarsoft’s portfolio.
items.summary: Focuses on building modeling and documentation rather than plain 2D drafting; interoperability expectations should be validated against IFC/DWG exchange needs of your project. Use the GstarBIM user guide PDFs from the vendor help hub for version-specific scope.

items.name: Houseplan
items.tagline: Fast residential massing and presentation with real-time rendering as positioned on the vendor site.
items.summary: Targets users who need quick 3D schemes rather than full mechanical CAD. Feature depth and file exchange differ from GstarCAD—treat it as a separate lane when planning tutorials and deliverables.

items.name: DWG FastView
items.category_label: Cloud & cross-platform DWG viewer / light editor
items.tagline: Browser, mobile, and desktop clients to open, annotate, and share DWG without a full CAD seat.
items.summary: Anchored at en.dwgfastview.com—useful for field markup, investor reviews, and quick measurement. Editing depth is intentionally narrower than desktop GstarCAD; check SDK/licensing separately if you embed viewers in your own apps.

items.name: DWG FastView Plus
items.tagline: Desktop viewer positioned as an alternative light client for plotting and reviewing DWGs on Windows.
items.summary: Often used when full authoring is unnecessary but fidelity and speed matter for QA. Verify download source (vendor-linked CadWonder endpoints) and version against your DWG baseline.

items.name: 3D FastView
items.tagline: Separate 3D viewing line for heavyweight CAD/visualization workloads linked from Gstar marketing.
items.summary: Use when assemblies or STEP/IGES-heavy workflows need navigation beyond 2D DWG scope. Licensing and supported formats evolve—confirm on vendor pages before standardizing workflows.
